title: PaperLab
pitch: Type a sentence and watch it travel through one layer of the Transformer from Attention Is All You Need.
problem: Papers explain attention in equations that few people can picture.
build: A React and TypeScript app that runs real attention math on toy weights in the browser, with per-head heatmaps and step controls.
result: 19 unit tests on the math and about 58 KB gzipped.
imageAlt: PaperLab showing an attention heatmap for a typed sentence, with step controls beside it.

screens.alt: PaperLab input panel with a typed sentence, preset sentences, the token counter and the four-step stepper.
screens.caption: The input. A sentence goes in, the token counter shows the 16-token cap, and the stepper walks the four stages.

screens.alt: Two heatmaps: token embeddings and the sinusoidal positional encoding, one row per token and 16 columns.
screens.caption: Step 2. Embeddings plus the sinusoidal position wave from section 3.5 of the paper.

screens.alt: The feed-forward step with its formulas and the first matrix after attention and layer norm.
screens.caption: Step 4. The feed-forward block, the residual and layer norm, with the formula above the numbers.

title: Online Paluwagan
pitch: A demo rotating-savings group with a reconciling ledger, a seeded payout draw, and pre-written reminder templates a person approves before anything is sent.
problem: Paluwagan groups run on chat threads and memory, so late payments and disputes are common.
build: An append-only ledger in integer centavos, a seeded payout draw, rule-based risk flags, and pre-written reminder templates in English and Filipino that a person approves.
result: 56 tests, including 12,000 random ledger operations, arrears included, that reconcile in every run so far.
imageAlt: Online Paluwagan group dashboard showing the ledger, payout rotation, and payment status.

screens.alt: Contributions by cycle for cycle 4: members paid on time, paid late, or not recorded, with Record buttons.
screens.caption: Contributions for one cycle. Late and missing payments are visible at a glance.

screens.alt: The append-only ledger table with entry numbers, types, members, signed amounts and Reverse buttons.
screens.caption: The ledger. Entries are never edited. A mistake gets a reversing entry instead.

screens.alt: Risk cards for two members marked High risk, with reasons and an arrears-owed panel.
screens.caption: Risk flags with their reasons, and the arrears a short payout created.

resultSource: `npm run evidence` in paluwagan, 56 passed, 12,000 operations counted by src/domain/ledger.test.ts, 2026-10-28

title: Living Mindmap (MCP)
pitch: A mind map I edit by hand and AI agents extend through 12 MCP tools. It refuses near-duplicates and marks every node an agent adds.
problem: Ideas from long AI conversations vanish into chat history.
build: One SQLite store shared by a React Flow UI, a REST API, and a stdio MCP server with near-duplicate detection.
result: 42 tests and 0 failures across 160 real MCP calls.
imageAlt: Living Mindmap canvas showing a sample graph of 16 connected nodes about Transformers, with a side panel of shortcuts.

screens.alt: The sample map on the canvas: Transformers at the root with branches for attention, position, architecture and training.
screens.caption: The bundled sample map laid out as a tree. Every node is a row in one SQLite file.

screens.alt: The inspector open on the Self-Attention node with status, summary and notes fields.
screens.caption: The inspector. People edit here and agents edit the same record through MCP.

screens.alt: The search box with results for attention, each showing a title and a summary snippet.
screens.caption: Search across maps. The MCP tool search_nodes runs the same query.

resultSource: `npm run evidence` in mindmap-mcp, 42 passed, bench calls=160 with 0 failures, 2026-10-28

title: Slop Editorial
pitch: A satire of AI content sites, with fake metrics and fake upsells. Behind it is a real image pipeline that will not spend money without approval.
proves: A paid pipeline that asks before it spends
problem: AI makes images nearly free, so publications drift into content that nobody decided to make.
build: A Python pipeline that estimates, caps, approves, and logs every paid generation, plus an Astro and Three.js site whose build gates enforce voice, honesty, links, and speed.
result: 70 unit tests across the pipeline and the site, 143 real-browser checks, and 146 build gates.
imageAlt: Slop Editorial home page: a too-perfect synthetic sunset titled The Still with a Free, limited availability sticker and a rank badge.

screens.alt: The release tracker headed Your November is 17 % approved, with six sample releases and their states.
